newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LION NATHAN TO CARRY EXTRA AUSTRALIA TAX.
newsitem.headline: LION NATHAN TO CARRY EXTRA AUSTRALIA TAX.

text.p: New Zealand-based brewer Lion Nathan Ltd said on Thursday it would not pass on to its trade customers any price rises arising from higher taxes following the High Court excise judgment last week.
The company, a distant second to Foster's Brewing Group Ltd in the Australian beer market, said its decision to compensate retailers had been backdated to August 6.

It said it had sent a proposal to the national government and anti-monopolies body that would result in no rise in wholesale prices for low alcohol and regular beers following the ruling which found that state and territory franchise fees were un constitutional.
The government plans a 15 percent rise in the wholesale sales tax to compensate the states for the lost income from beer and tobacco excises.

Lion Nathan, which has about 41 percent of the national market, said it estimated the tax rise now facing the industry was A$20 million but it would not pass on any increases until the impasse between the states and federal government over the tax issue had been settled.
